themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints in Bed-Stuy spiked to 6 reports THIS WEEK compared to a baseline average of 1.0 per week (500% increase, z-score: 4.47), signaling either a genuine uptick in street-level drug dealing or increased community reporting of visible drug activity.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike)
Z-score of 4.47 indicates statistically significant deviation
Coincides with recent fatal shooting of 7-month-old in district (Gothamist, 2026-04-14), suggesting possible neighborhood violence escalation
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct captain about enforcement response and whether spike reflects new dealing activity or improved community reporting
Canvass affected blocks to document resident safety concerns and whether residents feel police presence has changed

themes_detail.label: Public Urination Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Public urination complaints exploded to 3 reports 2 weeks ago (April 7–13) versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical severity)—suggesting either a specific location issue, homeless encampment, or sanitation breakdown.
evidence: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69—highest severity in dataset)
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for homeless services and health/safety inspections
May indicate specific geographic cluster worth geo-mapping from 311 data
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 3 complaints to identify if they cluster on one block or transit hub; interview businesses/residents about what they're observing
Contact Department of Homeless Services to ask if they've identified new encampment activity in the district; cross-reference with outreach data

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 4 reports last week versus a baseline of 0.6 per week (540% increase, z-score: 4.85), suggesting potential food safety violations or a contaminated food source in the district.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% spike)
Community board has repeatedly requested increased health inspections for restaurants and food establishments
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details to identify which restaurants/food vendors appear in reports; cross-reference with DOHMH inspection records
Interview complainants to establish timeline and common source (shared restaurant, catering event, food vendor)

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints spiked to 16 reports 2 weeks ago compared to a baseline of 3.2 per week (392% increase, z-score: 6.88), indicating residents are calling 311 about police-adjacent issues at elevated rates, warranting investigation into what types of incidents are driving the surge.
evidence: 16 non-emergency police complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (392% increase)
Z-score of 6.88 indicates strong statistical signal
Overlaps temporally with drug activity spike and fatal shooting of 7-month-old girl in district
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint categories/descriptions to understand whether complaints are about crime-in-progress, quality-of-life enforcement, or police conduct
Interview NYPD about call volume and response patterns; ask whether precinct has heightened enforcement operations in effect

themes_detail.label: Environmental/Lot Blight Surge
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints jumped to 7 reports 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.8 per week (833% increase, z-score: 4.49), alongside a 471% spike in dumpster complaints (5 vs. 0.9 baseline, z-score: 5.28) and 172% rise in sidewalk condition complaints, suggesting deteriorating street-level environmental conditions.
evidence: Lot condition: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% spike)
Dumpster complaints: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% spike)
Sidewalk condition: 17 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.2 weekly average (172% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Combined signal suggests concentrated environmental degradation or service gap
reporting_angles: Geo-map all three complaint types to see if they cluster on same blocks; visit those locations to document blight conditions on camera
Interview Sanitation Department about collection schedules, street cleaning frequency, and whether staffing has changed; ask about deferred maintenance
